reconstructed_theorem_text: Let Ω be a measurable space, let μ be a measure on Ω, and let B assign to every nonnegative real time a real-valued random variable on Ω. Assume that B satisfies IsPreBrownianReal B μ. For every n ∈ ℕ and every monotone map times : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ≥0 (with repeated grid points allowed), write Δtᵢ = times(i.succ) − times(i.castSucc) in ℝ≥0 and ΔBᵢ(ω) = B(times(i.succ), ω) − B(times(i.castSucc), ω). If Q(ω) = ∑ i : Fin n, ((ΔBᵢ(ω))² − (Δtᵢ : ℝ)), then ∫ ω, Q(ω)² ∂μ = 2 · ∑ i : Fin n, ((Δtᵢ : ℝ))².
objects: A measurable sample space Ω; a measure μ on Ω; a process B indexed by nonnegative real times and taking real values on Ω; a natural number n; an ordered deterministic time grid times with n + 1 entries; the grid-cell increments ΔBᵢ and elapsed times Δtᵢ; and the quadratic-variation error Q.
domains: B has time domain ℝ≥0 and consists of real-valued random variables on Ω. The index n lies in ℕ. The grid is times : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ≥0. Cell indices lie in Fin n. The integration variable ω lies in Ω. Each Δtᵢ is formed in ℝ≥0 and then coerced to ℝ in the displayed equality.
quantifiers: Universally quantified over B and μ through the ambient theorem variables, then conditional on hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ; universally quantified over n : ℕ and times : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ≥0, conditional on hmono : Monotone times. The equality covers every ω through integration and every i : Fin n through the finite sums.
assumptions: The sample space is measurable and μ is a measure. IsPreBrownianReal B μ supplies centered Gaussian increments whose variances equal their elapsed times, together with independence of increments on ordered deterministic grids. The map times is monotone. Repeated grid points are permitted. Subtraction in ℝ≥0 is truncated subtraction, and monotonicity ensures it represents the nonnegative elapsed time on each cell.
conclusion: The μ-integral of the square of the full quadratic-variation error along the grid equals twice the sum of the squared cell lengths: ∫ ω, (quadraticVariationError B times ω)² ∂μ = 2 · ∑ i : Fin n, (((times i.succ − times i.castSucc : ℝ≥0) : ℝ))².
scopes: The outer square on the left applies to the entire finite sum defining the quadratic-variation error, and the integral is over ω with respect to μ. On the right, the sum ranges over i : Fin n and each square applies only to the real coercion of that cell's elapsed time. The coefficient 2 multiplies the whole finite sum. The monotonicity assumption has scope over the complete grid and therefore every adjacent cell.
constant_dependencies: The numerical coefficient 2 is universal and depends on none of B, μ, n, times, i, or ω; it is the Gaussian variance factor for a centered squared increment after subtracting its mean. The right-hand side depends only on n and the grid times. The left-hand side depends on B, μ, n, and times. Zero-length cells contribute zero, so allowing repeated grid points introduces no extra term.
